reasoning: The agent reached a complete, valid, and faithful result in five calls on a four-field form, and every value it wrote came from the goal or from a tool response rather than from invention. Without a getSchema tool it oriented itself with describeState, whose output was accurate and sufficient: it named all four paths, marked /name and /email required-and-erroring, gave the English labels the French-free goal needed to map onto, exposed the numeric constraints on /birthYear (min=1800, max=2100, step=1, precision=0 — a faithful rendering of the integer/minimum/maximum schema), and flagged /contactMethod as a select with suggestions. That flag is what made the one genuinely information-buying follow-up call obvious: getFieldSuggestions on /contactMethod returned the closed list email/phone/post, so the agent's choice of "email" for "prefers to be contacted by email" was read off the form rather than guessed at. It then wrote the whole object in a single setData, which answered "valid, no errors". No path was guessed wrongly, no response was true-but-misleading, no error had to be recovered from, and the round-trip count is essentially what the protocol requires: one orientation, one enum read, one write. The only slack is two low-value reads bracketing the run.

friction.inferred: The agent learned the form was empty and invalid but nothing about why or what fields exist, so it had to call describeState next regardless; the call bought no information that call 2 did not supply.
